steps.title: Equipment & Benefits Logistics

Statutory pension contribution where the employer pays two-thirds of the total.

rows.label: Holiday Allowance

Depending on if the employee is salaried or paid hourly, covering 25 days of annual leave.

rows.label: Sickness Benefit Fund

Salaried employees receive full pay during sickness; employers can apply for reimbursement after 30 days.

rows.label: Maternity/Paternity

items.title: The Salaried Employees Act
items.text: Most white-collar workers are protected by 'Funktionerloven', which defines strict rules for notice periods and sickness.

items.title: CBAs vs. Individual Contracts
items.text: Even if your company isn't part of a CBA, many local hires expect terms that align with the major industry agreements (e.g., DI/CO-Sø).

items.title: Notice Period Scaling
items.text: Notice starts at 1 month and scales with seniority. Terminating a long-term employee can require up to 6 months of notice.

items.title: The 120-Day Rule
items.text: Contracts can include a clause allowing termination with 1 month notice if an employee has 120 days of paid sick leave in 12 months.

items.title: Holiday Act (Ferieloven)
items.description: Employees earn 2.08 days of holiday monthly. The period for taking holiday runs from September to December of the following year.

items.title: Trial Periods (Prøvetid)
items.description: Standard trial periods are 3 months, during which termination notice is typically 14 days for the employer.

items.title: Working Hours
items.description: While 37 hours/week is the standard full-time norm, the legal maximum is 48 hours over a 7-day period on average.

items.title: Termination Formalities
items.description: All terminations must be objectively justified to avoid claims of unfair dismissal, especially for protected groups.

items.title: Flat Hierarchy
items.description: Danish culture values egalitarianism. Employees expect to be consulted and involved in decision-making processes.

items.title: Work-Life Balance
items.description: Denmark consistently ranks high for work-life balance. Overtime is rare and usually compensated or given as time off.

items.title: Flat-Rate Expat Tax
items.description: Highly paid foreign recruits may qualify for the 27% researcher/expat tax scheme—a major draw for international talent.

faqs.question: Can I hire contractors through an EOR in Denmark?
faqs.answer: Yes, EORs can help manage contractor compliance, ensuring they aren't 'misclassified' as employees under Danish law.

faqs.question: What is the standard 'Holidays with Pay' percentage?
faqs.answer: For those not receiving salary during holiday, employers pay 12.5% of the qualifying salary into the Holiday Account (Feriekonto).

faqs.question: Is severance pay mandatory in Denmark?
faqs.answer: Under the Salaried Employees Act, 1 month salary is due after 12 years of service, and 3 months after 17 years.

faqs.question: Do I need to provide a pension scheme?
faqs.answer: Outside of CBAs, private pensions are optional but highly standard (typically 8-10% employer contribution).

steps.title: Variable Data Collection

steps.title: Gross-to-Net Calculation

steps.title: eIndkomst Reporting

items.title: eIndkomst Reporting
items.text: All payroll data must be reported digitally to the national system. Retrospective changes require specific correction codes.

items.title: Skatteministeriet Audits
items.text: The Danish tax authorities frequently audit payroll records to ensure correct withholding and AM-bidrag reporting.

items.title: Holiday Pay Liability
items.text: Accrued holiday pay for salaried workers (1% allowance) represents a real financial liability that must be tracked monthly.

items.title: NemKonto Requirement
items.text: Salary payments should ideally be made to the employee's NemKonto to ensure compliance with government banking standards.

items.title: ATP Pension Payments
items.description: ATP contributions are paid quarterly. Failure to pay on time results in significant interest penalties.

items.title: Digital Payslips
items.description: Danish law mandates that employees receive a specification of their salary and deductions, usually delivered electronically.

items.title: Tax Card Priority
items.description: If a tax card is unavailable, the employer MUST withhold 55% in tax—making rapid Skattekort retrieval critical.

items.title: Retention of Records
items.description: Payroll records and supporting documentation must be stored securely for at least 5 years under the Danish Bookkeeping Act.

faqs.question: What is the payroll deadline in Denmark?
faqs.answer: The most common pay date is the last banking day of the month, with reporting typically due multiple times throughout the cycle.

faqs.question: Are bonuses taxed differently?
faqs.answer: No, bonuses are treated as ordinary earned income and are subject to the same AM-bidrag and A-tax withholding.

faqs.question: Can we pay in EUR?
faqs.answer: While contracts can specify EUR, the actual payment and tax reporting must usually be calculated in DKK for the local authorities.

faqs.question: Is 13th-month pay required?
faqs.answer: No, 13th-month pay is not standard or legally required in Denmark, though performance bonuses are common.

steps.title: AM-bidrag Application

items.title: Tax Card Precision
items.text: Net pay calculations are only as accurate as the' Skattekort' (tax card) data provided by the employee.

items.title: NemKonto Integration
items.text: Ensure your calculator assumes payment to a NemKonto, as this is the standard for almost all Danish payouts.

items.title: Benefits in Kind
items.text: Remember that free phone, company car, or internet are taxable and must be added back into the gross logic.

items.title: Church Tax (Kirkeskat)
items.text: Typically ~0.7%, this is optional and depends on the employee's membership in the Danish State Church.

items.title: Currency Support
items.description: The calculator must default to DKK (Danish Krone) for statutory reporting accuracy.

items.title: Update Frequency
items.description: Logic must be updated annually (usually in Jan) to reflect new tax thresholds and municipality rates.

items.title: Pension Logic
items.description: Supports both fixed amount and percentage-based occupational pension contributions.

items.title: Data Privacy
items.description: Salary simulations are sensitive; ensure no PII (Personally Identifiable Information) is stored during the calc.

faqs.question: Does it calculate 'Topskat'?
faqs.answer: Yes, the logic includes the additional 15% tax for income exceeding the annual threshold (~600k DKK).

faqs.question: Can I calculate hourly wages?
faqs.answer: Yes, most calculators allow switching between monthly fixed salary and hourly rate conversions.

faqs.question: Are deductions for lunch included?
faqs.answer: Custom fields allow for non-taxable deductions like company canteen schemes.

faqs.question: Is the output legally binding?
faqs.answer: No, calculators provide a high-precision estimate, but the final payslip from an authorized payroll provider is the legal record.

steps.title: Articles of Association

steps.title: Capital Deposit & Verification

items.title: The Virk.dk Portal
items.text: Denmark is highly digitized. Almost all company management tasks are handled via the central Virk.dk business portal.

items.title: MitID for Managers
items.text: Managing directors and board members must obtain a personal MitID to sign official company documents digitally.

items.title: Bank Account Challenges
items.text: Opening a business bank account can be time-consuming due to strict KYC/AML processes. Start this early.

items.title: Branch vs Subsidiary
items.text: Foreign companies often choose a subsidiary (ApS) over a branch for easier administration and limited liability.

items.title: Local Address
items.description: A Danish company must have a physical registered office address in Denmark (P.O. boxes are not sufficient).

items.title: Management Board
items.description: An ApS can have just one executive director; an A/S must have an executive board and a board of directors.

items.title: Digital Mailbox (e-Boks)
items.description: All Danish companies are required to have a digital mailbox (Digital Post) for communicating with authorities.

items.title: Statutory Records
items.description: Companies must maintain a register of shareholders and meeting minutes, which must be kept for at least 5 years.

faqs.question: How long does it take to register a company?
faqs.answer: With digital filing, a CVR number can often be issued within 24 to 48 hours, though bank setup takes longer.

faqs.question: Can a foreigner own 100% of a Danish company?
faqs.answer: Yes, there are no restrictions on foreign ownership for most business sectors in Denmark.

faqs.question: Is a resident director required?
faqs.answer: No, directors do not need to be Danish residents, but they must be reachable and have valid identification.

faqs.question: Can I use intellectual property as share capital?
faqs.answer: Yes, 'contributions in kind' (like IP or equipment) are allowed but require a formal valuation report from an auditor.

heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Staffing in Denmark
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Staffing in Denmark.

steps.title: Profile Benchmarking
steps.description: Defining roles with a focus on both technical skills and cultural fit for flat Danish organizational structures.

steps.title: Multi-Channel Sourcing
steps.description: Leveraging LinkedIn (dominant in Denmark), local job boards like Jobindex, and university networks.

steps.title: Competency-Based Interviews
steps.description: Conducting interviews that prioritize autonomy, problem-solving, and collaboration over pure hierarchy.

steps.title: Reference & Qualification Check
steps.description: Verifying educational credentials and contacting previous employers, which is a standard part of the Danish vetting process.

steps.title: Offer & Contract Negotiation
steps.description: Finalizing salary packages, notice periods, and benefit expectations to ensure long-term retention.

items.title: The 'Flexicurity' Model
items.text: Denmark's model combines easy hiring/firing with high social security, creating a dynamic and fluid labor market.

items.title: English Profficiency
items.text: Denmark consistently ranks in the top 5 globally for non-native English proficiency, making it ideal for international teams.

items.title: Scarcity of Tech Talent
items.text: Developer roles are in high demand. Expect to provide competitive packages and flexible work arrangements.

items.title: Employee Autonomy
items.text: Danish employees value 'self-management' and high levels of responsibility. Micromanagement is highly counter-productive.

items.title: Equal Treatment Act
items.description: Danish law strictly prohibits discrimination based on gender, race, religion, age, or sexual orientation during hiring.

items.title: GDPR in Recruitment
items.description: Applicant data must be handled according to strict GDPR guidelines, including clear retention policies.

items.title: Non-Compete Clauses
items.description: Restrictive covenants are strictly regulated and often require compensation to the employee during the restricted period.

items.title: Criminal Record Checks
items.description: While common for certain sectors (finance, childcare), employers must have a legitimate reason to request a Børneattest.

items.title: The 'Jante Law'
items.description: While fading, a cultural emphasis on humility means talent often undersells themselves compared to US or UK standards.

items.title: Direct Communication
items.description: Danes are known for being direct and honest in feedback. This is seen as efficiency, not rudeness.

items.title: Social Integration
items.description: Workplace 'hygge' and social events (Friday bars) are important for team cohesion and employee satisfaction.

faqs.question: What are typical recruitment fees?
faqs.answer: Standard agency fees range from 15% to 25% of the annual gross salary, with guarantees usually covering the first 3-6 months.

faqs.question: Are background checks standard?
faqs.answer: Basic reference checks are standard. Credit checks (RKI) are only allowed for positions involving significant financial responsibility.

faqs.question: How long is the standard notice period?
faqs.answer: For salaried employees, it starts at 1 month (employer to employee) and increase by 1 month for every 3 years of service.

faqs.question: Do candidates expect remote work?
faqs.answer: Yes, hybrid work models are now standard in most office-based industries in Copenhagen and Aarhus.

heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to HRIS in Denmark

steps.title: Requirement Mapping
steps.description: Identifying specific local needs like SKAT eIndkomst integration and ferieloven (holiday) tracking.

steps.title: GDPR Compliance Setup
steps.description: Configuring data access levels and retention policies to meet Datatilsynet standards.

steps.title: Digital Onboarding Flow
steps.description: Setting up paperless contract signing and document collection via secure portals.

steps.title: Employee Self-Service
steps.description: Launching accessible modules for leave requests, expense claims, and personal data updates.

steps.title: Payroll Bridge Integration
steps.description: Ensuring a seamless data flow between the HRIS and the monthly payroll processing engine.

items.title: Holiday Act Automation
items.text: The 2020 Holiday Act is complex (accrue & take concurrently). Your HRIS MUST be able to handle this automatically.

items.title: MitID Integration
items.text: Advanced Danish HR systems often integrate with MitID for ultra-secure employee authentication and signing.

items.title: Data Residency
items.text: While most global SaaS is fine, ensure your provider has a clear DPA (Data Processing Agreement) covering Danish employees.

items.title: Mobile First Adoption
items.text: Danish workers are highly tech-savvy and expect to manage their HR tasks via mobile apps on the go.

items.title: Right to Erasure
items.description: System must support the 'Right to be Forgotten' for ex-employees, excluding data required by the Bookkeeping Act.

items.title: Audit Logs
items.description: To meet security standards, the system must log all access to sensitive personal and salary data.

items.title: Digital Document Storage
items.description: All employment documents should be stored in a central, encrypted digital repository, not on local drives.

items.title: API Capabilities
items.description: Modern Danish HRIS solutions require open APIs to connect with local payroll providers and time-tracking apps.

items.title: User Experience (UX)
items.description: High design expectations mean that 'clunky' legacy systems often face low adoption rates in Denmark.

items.title: Language Support
items.description: While English is fine for management, employees appreciate having the front-end interface available in Danish.

items.title: Training & Support
items.description: Allocate budget for training sessions to ensure all staff understand how to use the self-service features effectively.

faqs.question: Can we use global HRIS like Workday in Denmark?
faqs.answer: Yes, but you often need a local middleware or specific configuration to handle Danish 'Concurrent Holiday' rules.

faqs.question: How do we handle PDPA/GDPR?
faqs.answer: A modern HRIS centralizes consent and data policy management, making it much easier to stay compliant than using spreadsheets.

faqs.question: Does it support local time-off types?
faqs.answer: Yes, systems should be configured for 'barnets første sygedag' (child's first sick day) and other local custom entitlements.

faqs.question: Is digital signature legally binding?
faqs.answer: Yes, digital signatures (especially those using MitID or advanced e-signatures) are fully recognized by Danish courts.

rows.label: VAT (Standard)

Mandatory if revenue >12m DKK, assets 4m DKK, or >12 average staff.

rows.label: Late Filing Penalty
values: Daily or flat-rate penalties for late submission of the annual report.

items.title: Digital Bookkeeping Act
items.text: Recent legislation mandates 100% digital bookkeeping and storage for most companies by 2025/2026.

items.title: XBRL Reporting
items.text: All annual reports must be filed in XBRL format via the Erhvervsstyrelsen (Danish Business Authority) portal.

items.title: Expense Deductibility
items.text: Danish tax law has strict rules on 'representation' (client meals/entertainment) deductibility, often capped at 25%.

items.title: TastSelv Erhverv

items.title: Retention Period

items.title: Auditor Requirement
items.description: Small companies can opt-out of audit if they stay below specific revenue/asset/staff thresholds for two years.

items.title: Interim Dividends
items.description: Danish law allows for interim dividends if the company has sufficient reserves and an interim balance sheet is prepared.

items.title: Consolidated Accounts
items.description: Parent companies may need to prepare consolidated group accounts depending on the size of the overall group.

faqs.question: When is the annual report deadline?
faqs.answer: The annual report must be received by the Danish Business Authority no later than 6 months after the end of the financial year.

faqs.question: Can we keep books in EUR?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the annual report must still include specific figures in DKK, and the functional currency must be justified.

faqs.question: What is the VAT registration threshold?
faqs.answer: Registration is mandatory if revenue from taxable activities exceeds 50,000 DKK within a 12-month period.

faqs.question: Do we need an auditor for a new ApS?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily for a small startup, as you can often opt-out of audit during the incorporation process if you meet the criteria.

steps.title: Entity Health Check
steps.description: Ensuring the CVR registration is active and all board details are up to date.

steps.title: Statutory Filings
steps.description: Scheduling annual report submissions and UBO (Ultimate Beneficial Owner) updates.

steps.title: GDPR Compliance Audit
steps.description: Reviewing data processing agreements and employee privacy notices.

steps.title: Work Environment Compliance
steps.description: Ensuring the Arbejdspladsvurdering (APV) or workplace assessment is conducted every 3 years.

steps.title: Insurance Verification
steps.description: Confirming mandatory industrial injury insurance (Arbejdsskadeforsikring) is in place for all staff.

items.title: Digital First Government
items.text: Compliance is primarily managed through digital portals like Virk.dk and Erhvervsstyrelsen.

items.title: The 'APV' Obligation
items.text: Every company with even one employee MUST conduct a written workplace assessment (APV) every three years.

items.title: Whistleblower Requirements
items.text: Companies with 50 or more employees must establish an internal whistleblower scheme under Danish law.

items.title: Employment Protection
items.text: While 'flexicurity' allows for fluid hiring, compliance with the Salaried Employees Act is strictly enforced.

items.title: UBO Registration
items.description: All legal entities must register their real owners in the Public Register of Shareholders.

items.title: Industrial Injury Insurance
items.description: Employer-paid insurance for work-related accidents is mandatory and strictly regulated.

items.title: Holiday Act Transparency
items.description: Employers must accurately track and report 'concurrent' holiday entitlement for all workers.

items.title: Digital Post (e-Boks)
items.description: Compulsory digital mailbox for receiving official communication from Danish authorities.

faqs.question: What is the most important compliance portal?
faqs.answer: Virk.dk is the central entry point for almost all business-related filings and authority interactions.

faqs.question: Is an office audit common?
faqs.answer: The Working Environment Authority (Arbejdstilsynet) may conduct unannounced inspections to check APV and safety standards.

faqs.question: How do we handle GDPR for employees?
faqs.answer: You must maintain a processing record and provide a clear' Privacy Notice' to employees upon hiring.

faqs.question: What are the penalties for non-compliance?
faqs.answer: Fines vary but can be significant, especially for GDPR breaches or missing mandatory worker insurance.

rows.label: Industrial Injury Insurance

rows.label: External Secretary Service
values: Annual retainer for maintaining statutory registries and filings.

rows.label: APV Audit Vendor
values: One-time cost every 3 years for professional workplace assessment.

steps.title: Dividend Tax Withholding

steps.title: Annual Tax Settlement

rows.label: Corporate Income Tax
values: Standard flat rate for companies. Branches are taxed at the same rate.

rows.label: Dividend Tax

rows.label: Interest/Royalty WHT
values: Withholding tax on payments to non-residents in non-treaty countries.

rows.label: Hydrocarbon Tax
values: Specific tax applied to income from oil and gas extraction in Danish territory.

items.title: Expat Tax Scheme
items.text: Highly skilled foreign employees and researchers may qualify for a flat tax of ~32.84% for up to 7 years.

items.title: R&D Tax Incentives
items.text: Denmark offers a 'tax credit' for R&D costs, allowing loss-making companies to receive a cash refund of the tax value of R&D losses.

items.title: Controlled Foreign Company
items.text: CFC rules may apply if a Danish company has a controlling interest in a foreign subsidiary in a low-tax jurisdiction.

items.title: Joint Taxation
items.text: Danish group companies and Danish permanent establishments are subject to mandatory national joint taxation.

items.title: TastSelv Erhverv
items.description: The digital self-service for all business tax matters, requires MitID for access.

items.title: Tax Year
items.description: Usually follows the calendar year, but companies can apply for a different financial year.

items.title: Loss Carry-Forward
items.description: Tax losses can generally be carried forward indefinitely, but usage against high profits may be restricted.

items.title: Binding Rulings
items.description: Companies can request a binding ruling from SKAT for a fee to get certainty on the tax treatment of a specific transaction.

faqs.question: What is the corporate tax deadline?
faqs.answer: The tax return must be filed by June 27th for companies with a financial year ending Dec 31st.

faqs.question: Is there a capital gains tax?
faqs.answer: Capital gains on shares held by a company are often tax-exempt if specific ownership thresholds and periods are met.

faqs.question: Do we need to pay tax monthly?
faqs.answer: Corporate tax is paid in two voluntary installments (March and Nov), with a final adjustment the following year.

faqs.question: Does Denmark have many tax treaties?
faqs.answer: Yes, Denmark has an extensive network of double taxation treaties with almost 100 countries.

items.title: Prevalence of Mediation
items.text: Danish business culture prefers mediation and arbitration over lengthy and public court litigation.

items.title: Civil Law System
items.text: Denmark has a civil law system, but with strong Nordic traditions emphasizing pragmatism and fairness.

items.title: Mandatory Legislation
items.text: Danish law has several 'mandatory' provisions (e.g. in employment and tenancy) that cannot be waived by contract.

items.title: Digital Forensics
items.text: Digital evidence and e-discovery are well-integrated into the Danish legal process and accepted by courts.

items.title: Public Registry (CVR)
items.description: Basic company information, including ownership and management, is public record in Denmark.

items.title: Anti-Money Laundering

items.title: Power of Attorney

items.title: Insolvency Law
items.description: Danish law provides transparent procedures for reconstruction or bankruptcy, prioritizing creditor groups efficiently.

faqs.question: Is Danish law available in English?
faqs.answer: Many major acts have unofficial English translations provided by the ministries, though the Danish version remains authoritative.

faqs.question: Can we use UK or US law for contracts?
faqs.answer: Yes, freedom of contract allows this for B2B, but Danish mandatory rules (like employment) still apply to local operations.

faqs.question: What is a 'NemID' or 'MitID' signature?
faqs.answer: It is a highly secure, state-backed digital signature used for almost all legal and official transactions in Denmark.

faqs.question: How do we handle IP disputes?
faqs.answer: The Maritime and Commercial High Court in Copenhagen often handles complex IP and commercial disputes.

steps.title: Security & GDPR Review

values: Per user, per month for premium localized solutions.

items.title: High Digital Maturity
items.text: Denmark is among the most digitalized countries globally; users expect intuitive and mobile-first software.

items.title: MitID Integration
items.text: Software that handles sensitive data (HR, Finance) MUST offer MitID as a secure authentication method.

items.title: GDPR Sovereignty
items.text: Danish companies often prefer software with Tier-IV data centers located within the EU/EEA.

items.title: Local Language Support
items.text: While English is widely used, offering a Danish UI significantly increases adoption among diverse staff categories.

items.title: Data Portability
items.description: Ensuring you can export all your data in standard formats to avoid vendor lock-in.

items.title: API First Architecture
items.description: Prioritize software that allows seamless connectivity with existing Danish business ecosystems.

items.title: Uptime SLAs
items.description: Standard service level agreements for critical business software in Denmark expect 99.9% uptime.

items.title: Local Training
items.description: Providing training in Danish or during local working hours (08:00 - 16:00) is crucial for success.

faqs.question: Are cloud-based solutions common?
faqs.answer: Yes, nearly all Danish enterprises have shifted or are shifting to a cloud-first (SaaS) model.

faqs.question: What is the standard onboarding time?
faqs.answer: Simple SaaS tools take days, while complex ERP/HRIS systems can take 3 to 9 months for full deployment.

faqs.question: Can we use international software?
faqs.answer: Of course, but ensure it handles Danish nuances like unique tax reporting requirements (eIndkomst).

faqs.question: Is software development talent available?
faqs.answer: Denmark has a vibrant tech scene, but talent is highly competitive; many companies use hybrid local/remote teams.

steps.title: Market Resonance Research
steps.description: Analyzing Danish consumer trends and competitor positioning in the local market.

steps.title: Localization Strategy
steps.description: Adapting messaging, tone, and visual elements to align with Danish cultural nuances (e.g. anti-excess).

steps.title: Channel Selection
steps.description: Identifying the most effective platforms for reaching Danish audiences (LinkedIn for B2B, Instagram for B2C).

steps.title: Campaign Execution
steps.description: Launching multi-channel campaigns including social media, search engine marketing, and local PR.

steps.title: ROI Monitoring
steps.description: Tracking conversions and adjusting the strategy based on real-time data from the Danish market.

items.title: Trust & Transparency
items.text: Danish consumers place extreme importance on brand honesty and environmental sustainability.

items.title: Direct Communication
items.text: Avoid aggressive 'hard-sell' tactics. Danes prefer clear, functional, and value-driven messaging.

items.title: Strict Cookie Laws
items.text: Denmark enforces the GDPR and ePrivacy Directive strictly; ensure your consent banners are fully compliant.

items.title: Mobile First Audience
items.text: Over 90% of Danes use smartphones for shopping and social interaction; mobile optimization is non-negotiable.

items.title: Danish Translation
items.description: High-quality, native-level translation is crucial; automated translations are often seen as unprofessional.

items.title: Social Responsibility
items.description: Highlighting your company's 'Green' credentials or community involvement builds local trust.

items.title: Influencer Reach
items.description: Micro-influencers in Denmark have high engagement rates and are often more cost-effective for niche markets.

items.title: SEO (Danish Keywords)
items.description: Optimizing for Danish search terms and local 'vibe' is key to ranking on Google.dk.

faqs.question: What is the best platform for B2B?
faqs.answer: LinkedIn is almost universally used by the Danish professional workforce and is the primary B2B channel.

faqs.question: Is Google Ads expensive in Denmark?
faqs.answer: Competition is high across most sectors, leading to relatively high CPCs compared to Southern Europe.

faqs.question: Do Danes respond well to email marketing?
faqs.answer: Yes, but only if it's value-added and compliant with strict anti-spam regulations (explicit opt-in required).

faqs.question: How important is local PR?
faqs.answer: Gaining coverage in major outlets like Børsen or Politiken can provide massive instant credibility.
